round1.note: Sections 4.5 and 5.2 now carry non-resource rules as {nonResourceURLs, verbs, scope: CLUSTER} entries, sorted and deduplicated. Section 9 adds the nonResourceURLs ["*"] vector, and section 8 drops the residual. Which non-resource rules count (those reached through a RoleBinding) is still open: see D2-3.

Resolved by ruling R1-A. Section 4.4 admits only podSelector {} with peers by ipBlock alone and refuses every selector form. Section 8 says why no pod-label residual is needed, which R1-A asked for in place of round 1's residual.

Sections 4.6, 5.3 and 5.4 add capture gates, each with a refusal text and a vector. The R10 mapping is accurate: Taken is set only after check_capture, check_lifecycle_capture or check_backend_capture passes (R10:obs/capture.rs:519-537), inside a Current view. But section 3 binds the gates to 'the capture view current at that snapshot', so a set that fails after the snapshot does not withdraw the values: see D2-1.

Section 5.3 refuses when NETWORK_POLICY_AGENT, or its componentKeys member, is absent, with a refusal text and a section 9 vector, and the document does not rely on SERVICE_PROXY. REQUIRED_BACKEND is confirmed at R10:obs/record_check.rs:43.

Section 4.1 names the four sealed values and renders them with a2_objects and manifest_file_bytes under planeon-a2.json. Before emitting, it requires manifest_directory_hash to equal both the signed pin and ADM-4's loaded hash. No host read is added, and section 6 names the three values the configuration successor must carry.
All 20 members are listed, matching the schema. cgroup.inode is dropped together with namespaceInodes, and interpreterPath and interpreterLabel are explained as const null.

(a) apiVersion and kind are fixed per key. (b) There is one sort rule, canonical bytes, in both 3 and 5.3. (c) Integers are bounded by magnitude at 2^53 - 1. (d) The names are constants, and the namespaces are null or the configured namespace, never taken from the binding.

The subject set is defined by rule (RoleBindings in the namespace plus every ClusterRoleBinding, as OR03 does), rules are filtered by scope, schemaVersion is only in the closure value, and the vector is added. The subject key form and the closure entry's shape are still unstated: see D2-3.

There is a PCR row: each file is canonical(document) with no trailing newline, and the release author renders the synthetic ones. The release author and the capacity signer are named as readers, and the lifecycle is stated.
The complete positive carries its own derived profile. profileDigest, bindingDigest and request.bindingDigest are recomputed, and validate_profile is named.
PPV is registered at host-enforcement/contracts/i01-v1/proxy-contract-vectors.json, consumerPacket is HE-004-I01B, and PPS is not registered and is re-checked at build.

Section 4.1 refuses any listed ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or binding whose name lacks .static.k8s.io. The rule relies on the apiserver reserving that suffix, and the design does not state this: see D2-5.
Section 3 now covers labels and annotations. Section 4.3 refuses the enforce-mountable-secrets annotation, with a vector. A pruned git grep -l at 26a8affb finds no file that names the annotation.

R-ONE-NP is moved to scope, R-DEFAULTS has a per-kind T04 comparison, and D1-1 and D1-2 are no longer residuals. R-BROKER-LIVE still leaves out document members the BROKER capture does not observe (listenEndpointIds, outboundEndpointIds and executableLabel), and the network agent's record-only members have no residual at all: see D2-2.
Resolved by ruling R1-B. Section 4.2 cites I07 v3's default-deny vector and keeps Q-DIG-10 (b) for networkPolicy alone, through a contract revision.
There are two checks with two refusal texts, and vectors for zero objects, two objects and another name.
The no-spec rules for Role and RoleBinding and the RoleBinding subject sorting are dropped.
Section 6 states the record-profile relation and the order: capture, then profile, then record.
Sections 1 and 2 state that the README and definitions.json carry the CS, PV and RD sha256 pins.

findings.finding: The capture gates are anchored to the snapshot. Section 3 says they 'read the capture view current at that snapshot', section 6 says the observer recomputes 'at each snapshot', and section 11 builds the documents and digests from one snapshot under the gates. In R10 a snapshot lives long. It is replaced only when a watch shows an API change, a scrape escalates or the epoch restarts (R10:obs/observe.rs:1-60). A capture set, by contrast, runs every 60 s cycle, and a failing set is only a slot state that 'never ends the epoch' (R10:obs/observe.rs:36-41). So take a host change after the snapshot that the next set reports as Unavailable, for example the broker or network agent executable replaced. mutationBroker, the network document and hostPreflightDigest stay as computed, and the observer keeps answering with them until the next API-driven snapshot, which may never come on a quiet cluster. The text is also inconsistent: sections 4.6 and 5.4 say 'emitted only while', which reads the other way. Separately, R10's Current means only that the record's window is open (R10:obs/capture.rs:267-272; observe.rs:490-499). The contract sets no age bound on the set the gates read, so a view whose sets stopped running stays usable. Expired views and slots carried over from earlier sets are handled correctly (each set resets every slot first, R10:obs/capture.rs:1261).
findings.requiredChange: State that the capture gates hold at every answer, not only at the snapshot. Each capture-gated value (mutationBroker, the network document and networkEnforcementDigest, hostPreflightDigest) is emitted only while the latest set has the required slots Taken, and that set is younger than a stated bound, for example set_started_ms within one 60 s cycle plus the 25 s set budget of the answer. A later set without those slots withdraws the values until a set passes. Add two vectors: on one snapshot, a passing set followed by a failing set refuses; a set older than the bound refuses.

findings.finding: D1-14 asked R-BROKER-LIVE to list the document members the BROKER capture does not observe. It lists the image, the two seccomp members and the cgroup's selinuxLabel. It leaves out listenEndpointIds and outboundEndpointIds, which have no class row in HO:NP4R:150-158 and are not compared by check_capture (R10:obs/capture_check.rs:341-398, and grep finds no other comparison). It also leaves out executableLabel, a file label that is DECLARED_T04 under T04-LABELS (HO:NP4R:158) and is not named in the 'cannot see' column. The network document's agent object has the same gap and no residual at all. check_backend_capture is ENTRY_BOUND and compares only processLabel, cgroupPath and the executable's path, contentDigest and measuredVerity (R10:obs/capture_check.rs:613-635). So executableLabel, artifactDigest and apiIdentities are record values that the gate does not observe, and R-NET-DATAPATH names only the datapath and the flags.
findings.requiredChange: Add listenEndpointIds, outboundEndpointIds and executableLabel to R-BROKER-LIVE, each with its T04 or HE-005 check. Add the agent's executableLabel, artifactDigest and apiIdentities to R-NET-DATAPATH, or to a new R-NET-AGENT, with a T04 check, or drop them from the network document.

findings.finding: Three determinism gaps in the two RBAC documents. (1) The subject key is not fixed. R10's B1 names a ServiceAccount subject system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<name>, and a RoleBinding subject without a namespace takes the binding's (R10:obs/rbac.rs:202-219). That makes (kind, name) a total key. Revision 2 cites only B1's rule shape (:153-161). If the raw RBAC subject names are used instead, '(kind, name), then deduplicated' merges same-named ServiceAccounts from different namespaces, so a grant moved between them leaves both digests unchanged (Closure::check may still catch it). (2) Section 5.2 does not give the closure entry's members, for example whether exists is one, and does not say whether 'every subject in the cluster' means every bound subject (as in B1) or also unbound ServiceAccounts. (3) Section 4.5 adds 'its non-resource rules' with scope CLUSTER, but does not say whether rules reached through a RoleBinding count. The RBAC authorizer applies non-resource rules only through ClusterRoleBindings (Kubernetes behaviour, not a pinned source). As written, such a rule would enter rbac as CLUSTER even from a RoleBinding in another namespace. HE-008 and the observer could therefore compute different bytes for the same cluster.
findings.requiredChange: Fix the subject key as B1's: the ServiceAccount username form, with the RoleBinding namespace default. Fix the entry shape as {kind, name, exists, effectiveRules} in both documents, with exists defined as in B1. Define 'every subject' as every subject named by a RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding. Take non-resource entries from ClusterRoleBindings only, or give them the binding's scope. Add vectors for same-named ServiceAccounts in two namespaces and for a RoleBinding to a ClusterRole that holds nonResourceURLs.

findings.finding: R1-C's labels are covered, but PodSecurity's effect also depends on the apiserver's PodSecurity configuration: its defaults and its exemptions for usernames, runtimeClasses and namespaces (Kubernetes behaviour, not a pinned source). That configuration lives in the sealed admission configuration file (--admission-control-config-file, SC05 in HO:architecture/backend-distribution/selection.json). The observer cannot read that file, and the APISERVER backend capture checks only the executable. At 26a8affb no harness-onion file names a pod-security.kubernetes.io label or a PodSecurityConfiguration (pruned git grep -l), and I06 v2 leaves 'PodSecurity defaults' open (HO:docs/alpha-2/I06_BACKEND_PROFILE_V2.md:58, :63). So the release's podSecurityLabels is probably {}, and the namespace's level is exactly the configured default. An added exemption or a lowered default then changes enforcement with no digest change and no named residual, which the owner's frame does not allow. Pod Security labels on other namespaces are also outside every digest. The design cites N6's 'every namespace' but does not say these labels are outside the binding.
findings.requiredChange: Name a residual, for example R-PSA-CONFIG, for the PodSecurity defaults and exemptions in the sealed admission configuration, with a T04 check that compares them with the enrolled file. State that Pod Security labels on other namespaces are outside the I01 binding (I06 v2 N6, carried to W02f and W02e).

findings.finding: Section 4.1 lets through any listed ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or binding whose name ends in .static.k8s.io. That is safe only if the apiserver refuses API objects with that suffix. No pinned source states this, the design does not claim it, and R-ADM-LIST says list visibility is unknown. An API object with the suffix that predates the guard would pass as static. OR06, which section 4.1 says it mirrors, refuses every object of its four kinds (R10:obs/operational.rs:144-153). The impact is limited, because such an object can only add denials.
findings.requiredChange: Refuse any listed ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or binding whose name is not one of the eight rendered names. Add the suffix-reservation fact to R-ADM-LIST's T04 check, or cite a pinned source for it.

findings.finding: Selector-free forms still have two meanings that the document does not fix. An ipBlock whose CIDR overlaps the pod or Service ranges depends on which pod holds which IP, and the NetworkPolicy API leaves pod-IP behaviour to the implementation. A named port in ports resolves against pod container port names. Neither matters for v1: the bound policy is the default-deny form with no rules, so any added rule changes the digest. Still, section 4.4's 'whose meaning does not depend on any label' leaves the reader to work this out.
findings.requiredChange: In v1, either refuse named ports and ipBlocks that overlap the pod or Service CIDRs, or say in section 8 why they do not matter for the default-deny release.

findings.finding: Three citation details. (a) R10's configuration bounds integers to 0..2^53 - 1 (R10:obs/config.rs:7-9). VPC's _bounded bounds the magnitude instead (abs, HO:scripts/validate_proxy_contract.py:113-114), and the contract's rule is VPC's. (b) OR06 refuses every object of its four kinds, so section 4.1 mirrors it only in part, because of the suffix exemption. (c) I07 v3's default-deny NetworkPolicy is a writer vector (kindChecks[18], K19; the same spec is in kindChecks[19] and renderChecks[4]), not a release definition. PCR:320's 'zero external egress' is a native follow-up item.
findings.requiredChange: Cite VPC for the magnitude bound and say that negative integers within it are accepted. Say that OR06 is mirrored except for the static suffix. Describe K19 as the only NetworkPolicy form in I07 v3's vectors.

adversarialCases.where: The gates read the current set. R10 resets every slot to 'set budget' at the start of each set (R10:obs/capture.rs:1261) and replaces the view wholesale.

adversarialCases.case: A set where only some slots ran (the budget cut the rest)
adversarialCases.where: 5.4 needs every slot Taken. The observation needs all four digests (HO:VPO:129-130), so the narrower 4.6 and 5.3 gates cannot carry it alone.

adversarialCases.case: A host change after the snapshot (broker or network agent executable replaced) that the next set reports, on a quiet API with no re-snapshot
adversarialCases.where: 3: the gates read 'the capture view current at that snapshot', and 6 and 11 compute at the snapshot (D2-1)

adversarialCases.case: Capture sets stop running while the record's window is open (stale view)
adversarialCases.where: No age bound in the contract. R10's Current means only that the record window is open (D2-1). R10's 60 s cadence bounds it in practice.

adversarialCases.case: Sealed values that render to the pinned hash while the loaded directory holds a second file
adversarialCases.where: 4.1: the loader hash covers every non-empty .yaml, .yml or .json file's content followed by a NUL (HO:AS3M:481-490). Canonical JSON never holds a raw NUL, so only a single file equal to the rendered bytes matches. This depends on AS3's loader-hash fact.

adversarialCases.case: A configuration successor whose three sealed values differ from the release's
adversarialCases.where: 4.1: the rendered hash then differs from ADM-4's loaded hash. If the directory was also rendered from those values, the recomputed admissionFenceDigest and admissionPolicy digest differ from the release-pinned binding (HO:VPO:96-108, :129-130).

adversarialCases.case: A pod-security.kubernetes.io label added, removed or changed on the qualification namespace
adversarialCases.where: 4.1: podSecurityLabels is in admissionPolicy's digest. The Namespaces watch forces a new snapshot.

adversarialCases.case: A Pod Security label on another namespace (for example enforce: privileged)
adversarialCases.where: Not in any digest and not named. It is outside the I01 binding and affects only that namespace's pods, under I06 v2 N6 (carried to W02f). D2-4 asks for this to be stated.

adversarialCases.case: An exemption, or a lowered default, in the apiserver's PodSecurity configuration
adversarialCases.where: Unseen: it is in the sealed admission configuration file (SC05) and is not named as a residual (D2-4)

adversarialCases.case: An egress or ingress peer as ipBlock with except
adversarialCases.where: 4.4 admits it and it carries no label meaning, but any rule differs from the bound default-deny form, so the networkPolicy and network digests change. In-cluster CIDRs: D2-6.

adversarialCases.case: An ingress rule with no from (allow from all)
adversarialCases.where: 4.4 admits it, since the peer rule holds vacuously, and its meaning is label-free. The digest changes against the bound default-deny form.

adversarialCases.case: A policyTypes change (Egress dropped)
adversarialCases.where: The served spec is in the digest. Server defaulting is under R-DEFAULTS.

adversarialCases.case: A ClusterRoleBinding to a ClusterRole whose rules are namespaced
adversarialCases.where: B1 gives it scope CLUSTER (R10:obs/rbac.rs:323), so it enters both rbac (4.5) and the closure (5.2)

adversarialCases.case: A RoleBinding to a ClusterRole, in the qualification namespace and in another namespace
adversarialCases.where: The scope is the RoleBinding's namespace. In the qualification namespace it enters rbac and the closure; elsewhere it enters only the closure (5.2).

adversarialCases.case: A RoleBinding in another namespace that binds a ClusterRole holding nonResourceURLs
adversarialCases.where: There is no wrong pass under either reading, because Kubernetes ignores the rule. The two readings give different bytes, so HE-008 and the observer may disagree, which fails closed (D2-3).

adversarialCases.case: Non-resource rules duplicated or reordered across ClusterRoles to hide a change
adversarialCases.where: 3: rule lists are sorted and deduplicated by canonical bytes, so the result does not depend on ClusterRole order. A real change to the entries changes the bytes, and a reorder inside a rule fails closed.

adversarialCases.case: A grant moved between same-named ServiceAccounts in two namespaces
adversarialCases.where: Refused under B1's username key. Under raw names the subjects merge and the digests do not change. The contract does not fix the key (D2-3), and Closure::check may still refuse.

adversarialCases.case: An API-registered ValidatingAdmissionPolicy named with the .static.k8s.io suffix, created before the guard
adversarialCases.where: This holds unless the apiserver reserves the suffix, which is unpinned Kubernetes behaviour and was not checked (D2-5). Such an object can only add denials.

adversarialCases.case: Echo: the fixed identities (names, namespaces, uids) taken from the binding
adversarialCases.where: 3: constants, the configured namespace and derived uids. The binding is only compared against.

adversarialCases.case: Echo: the network agent's executableLabel, artifactDigest and apiIdentities taken from the record but not observed by the backend capture
adversarialCases.where: Record values behind an ENTRY_BOUND gate. Not named in R-NET-DATAPATH (D2-2).

adversarialCases.case: Echo: the BROKER document's listenEndpointIds, outboundEndpointIds and executableLabel taken from the record but not observed by the BROKER capture
adversarialCases.where: R-BROKER-LIVE's check column ends with HE-005 for behaviour, but the 'cannot see' column omits these members (D2-2)
